title: Aspatuck Creek
summary: A western Southampton creek name connected with Ketchaponack Neck, Quiogue, and older spellings including Aspatatuck and Assopatuck.
address_label: Aspatuck Creek near Westhampton and Quiogue, NY (approximate)
map_geometry_source: Approximate modern point from USGS monitoring location Aspatuck Creek Near Westhampton NY; not a full creek geometry.
why_this_matters: Aspatuck Creek preserves a Native waterway name in western Southampton between Ketchaponack Neck and Quiogue, even though no settled translation has been found. Its recorded forms show how English documents tried to represent a local name tied to creek, neck, and bay geography. Even uncertain placenames can mark real Indigenous relationships with waterways that shaped travel, foodways, and community memory.
introduction_content: Aspatuck is identified as a creek in western Southampton town, between Ketchaponack Neck and the locality once called Little Assups Neck, now known as Quiogue.
history_content: Early meadow divisions used the Aspatatuck form for land between Quantuck and Aspatatuck. Later forms include Aspatuck and Assopatuck, and a later Quiogue entry confirms Aspatuck as one boundary of that neck.
translation_content:
Recorded forms include Aspatatuck, Aspatuck, and Assopatuck but does not provide a settled translation in the available references. Aspatuck Creek should be kept distinct from neighboring land records for Quiogue, Quantuck, and Ketchaponack.

Why Place Names Matter

“Hence legends, guided chiefly by accidental resemblances between words, grow up to explain the origin of place-names whose real origin has been forgotten.”

— William F. Ganong, A Monograph of the Place-Nomenclature of the Province of New Brunswick (1896), Printed pp. 185–186; Internet Archive scan leaves n14–n15
whereintheworld_content: Aspatuck Creek marks how waterways organized meadow, neck, and boundary records in western Southampton. Keeping the creek separate from nearby neck names helps preserve the geography of the source records and keeps each place connected to its own landscape.
